heading: Native requests and responses
body: A Yon method that needs the whole request, or an answer with its own status and headers, uses the types of its own language (ADR 0062). The request is a Fetch `Request` in JavaScript and TypeScript, `urllib.request.Request` in Python, a `Net::HTTP` request in Ruby, `HttpExchange` in Java, Groovy and Kotlin, `HttpRequestMessage` in C# and F#, `http::Request<Vec<u8>>` in Rust, a shelf `Request` in Dart, `*http.Request` in Go and a table with `method`, `path`, `headers` and `body` in Lua. PHP has no request object: it reads `$_SERVER`, `$_GET`, `$_POST`, `$_COOKIE` and `php://input`. The answer is a Fetch `Response`, an `(HTTPStatus, headers, body)` tuple in Python, a `[status, headers, body]` array in Ruby and a `{ status, headers, body }` list in Lua, `http_response_code()`, `header()` and `echo` in PHP, a write on the same `HttpExchange` in Java, Groovy and Kotlin, `HttpResponseMessage` in C# and F#, `http::Response<Vec<u8>>` in Rust, a shelf `Response` in Dart and `*http.Response` in Go. A Go `*http.Response` body may hold binary bytes, such as an image or a file: Tachyon sends them unchanged. `YonRequest` and `YonResponse` are removed, and the build refuses them with a message that names the native type (TY2015). Tachyon itself uses private names that start with `__Yon` for the code it writes, so a `__Yon` name in your code is refused too. The server computes `content-length`, `transfer-encoding` and `connection`, so a handler answer does not set them. A Rust handler builds with Cargo and the `http` crate, offline first, so `ty doctor` checks for `cargo`. A Dart handler needs the `shelf` package: Tachyon writes a pubspec and runs `dart pub get`, which reads the pub cache or the network. PHP runs with `php-cgi`, the PHP program in which `header()` works. Homebrew's `php` includes it, Debian and Ubuntu have the `php-cgi` package, and the Windows PHP zip file has `php-cgi.exe`. `ty doctor` tells you when it is missing. The request ID is in the header `x-tachyon-request-id`. The client address is in `X-Real-IP`, and Go `RemoteAddr`, `HttpExchange.getRemoteAddress()` and PHP `$_SERVER['REMOTE_ADDR']` hold it too (see The client address and forwarding headers).
